Private objective: sum of your %1$s dice
Over ten rounds you fill a 5×4 window with dice. The player whose finished window scores highest wins. Play solo against one to three bots, or with three other people on the same network.

You get one private objective — a secret colour. At the end you add up the values of every die of that colour in your window.\n\nThree public objectives are shared by everyone and reward patterns, like a row where all five colours differ.

Each round rolls two dice per player plus one spare into the draft pool. Everyone takes one turn in order, then a second turn back down the order, so the last player takes two in a row. On each turn place one die or pass. The starting player rotates every round.
The first die you ever place must sit on an outside edge or corner of the window.\n\nAfter that, every die must touch a die already placed — side by side or diagonally.

A coloured cell accepts only that colour. A numbered cell accepts only that value. Clear cells accept any die.\n\nTwo dice that touch side by side may not share a colour or a value. Diagonal neighbours may match freely.

Add up every completed public objective, then add the values of dice matching your private colour. Subtract one point for every cell you left empty.\n\nIf two players tie, the higher private-objective score wins.

Tap a die in the draft pool and the legal cells light up gold. Tap one to place it. Tap the arrows to inspect any player\'s window, and the objective cards for a reminder of what they reward.\n\nThe ? button reopens this guide at any time without leaving your match.
